question.text: Konark Growth Fund (Cat II): Capital called INR 120 crore. Cumulative distributions to LPs (DPI cash out) = INR 144 crore. Residual NAV (unrealised) = INR 96 crore. Compute TVPI.

explanation.text: The Logic: TVPI (Total Value to Paid-In) = (Distributions + Residual NAV) / Capital Called = (INR 144 + INR 96) / INR 120 = INR 240 / INR 120 = 2.00x. DPI alone = 144/120 = 1.20x; RVPI alone = 96/120 = 0.80x; TVPI = DPI + RVPI = 2.00x. The Trap: A is DPI; C is RVPI; D mis-adds ratios. Cross-Exam Context: TVPI/DPI/RVPI are universal PE metrics — tested at XIX-A, XIX-C. PMS (XXI-B) uses different metrics (TWRR) since it handles listed liquid portfolios. Manager's Pro-Tip: LPs track the DPI-to-TVPI gap carefully: a fund at 2x TVPI but only 0.5x DPI is 'paper rich, cash poor'. Push for orderly realisations and don't rely on mark-to-market to float TVPI — LPs want cash.
